text:
Britain will add to its multimillion pound investments in rebuilding Ukraine’s energy system by funding a windfarm project capable of powering 300,000 Ukrainian households.
Ed Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, said Britain would invest £9.5m to build a 200 megawatt windfarm in an undisclosed location to bolster Ukraine’s energy reserves as its war with Russia approaches the five-year mark.
Kyiv believes Moscow’s strikes have destroyed or damaged more than 80% of Ukraine’s prewar power generation capacity, which was mostly fuelled by gas imported from Russia.
The UK government has offered more than £770m to rebuild Ukraine’s power system, which has included emergency support and long-term investments in renewables and nuclear generation to cut the country’s reliance on gas.
Ukraine is estimated to have installed more than 3GW of renewable energy capacity since the 2022 full-scale invasion, or 20% of the country’s installed generation capacity. About a third of that is from wind power.
Miliband said the money would help deliver “major new renewable generation, strengthen Ukraine’s energy independence and support its recovery, while deepening the economic partnership between our two countries”.
The new windfarm is expected to be built and operated by Elementum Energy, a company registered in the UK with offices in London, Kyiv and Odesa.
“While Russia seeks to plunge Ukrainians into darkness, the UK is helping Ukraine build the secure and resilient energy system it needs for the future,” Miliband said.
He set out the plans to help rebuild Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure within days of Moscow’s renewed attacks on the country’s energy system. On Wednesday, Russian strikes on a thermal power plant near Odesa in the south-west of Ukraine led to power, heating and water supply outages in parts of the city.
Ukraine’s largest private energy investor, DTEK, said that attack was the third massive strike against the company’s power plants in November alone as winter temperatures plunge.
DTEK became the first company to build a windfarm in a war zone when it completed the first phase of the Tyligulska project, generating enough clean electricity to power about 200,000 homes just 60 miles from the frontline in the southern region of Mykolaiv in early 2023.
The second phase of the Tyligulska plant was initially scheduled to be completed by the end of 2026.
digest_he:
בריטניה הודיעה על השקעה נוספת של 9.5 מיליון ליש"ט בשיקום מערכת האנרגיה של אוקראינה, הפעם באמצעות מימון פרויקט של חוות רוח בהספק של 200 מגה-וואט. הפרויקט צפוי לספק חשמל לכ-300 אלף משקי בית אוקראיניים ולחזק את עצמאותה האנרגטית של המדינה מול התקיפות הרוסיות.

שר החוץ הבריטי אד מיליבנד ציין כי ההשקעה נועדה לסייע בהתמודדות עם הפגיעה הקשה בתשתיות האנרגיה של אוקראינה, לאחר שקייב דיווחה כי תקיפות רוסיות הרסו או פגעו ביותר מ-80 אחוז מיכולת ייצור החשמל הקודמת שלה. את חוות הרוח תבקיע ותפעיל חברת Elementum Energy, המרכזת פעילות בתחום האנרגיה המתחדשת באזור.
